summary.intent: Drive the CipherBox v2 write-plane frontier forward: implement four unblocked issues (#861-#864) in parallel worktrees, ship each through the full verify/review/CI/PR pipeline, resolve merge-order conflicts between slices, and keep GitHub issue tracking (dependency edges, tracker checkboxes) in sync.
summary.outcome: All four issues (#861, #862, #863, #864) were implemented and #861/#862/#863 merged to main via PR #874, #877, #875; #864 (PR #878) passed CI and CodeRabbit review with fixes applied and is pending merge. Discovered and fixed two orphaned-issue/dependency-edge bugs and a lost-wake CodeRabbit-polling bug in the shared `.claude/commands/ship.md` skill, and corrected several stale tracker checkboxes.

repo: cipher-box uses GitHub native issue dependencies (blocked_by/blocking via API, not just prose 'Depends on #N') for tracker automation; ship-worker agents kept filing issues with only prose deps, believing that counted as tracking
Tracker issue #655 is a 55+ line manual markdown checklist; GitHub doesn't auto-tick it on issue close, so it must be patched manually after each merge
No build slice in this repo has a GitHub 'parent' issue — only wayfinder/design issues (e.g. #813) use sub-issues; slice-to-tracker relation is prose-only ('Part of #655') by convention
CodeRabbit PR review is rate-limited to ~1/hour org-wide and only triggers on PR-ready (not draft); this makes review-slot sequencing across concurrent PRs the real throughput bottleneck

The `Review rate limited` GitHub check status can be stale/frozen from a much earlier attempt and won't refresh until a new review is actually triggered — don't trust it to compute wait times, compute from the last known real review timestamp instead

Worktree agents lack node_modules, so commits there must use --no-verify (husky/lint-staged fails) with manual cargo fmt/clippy and prettier/markdownlint verification done from the main checkout afterward
cargo fmt must always run as `--all`, never `-p`, per repo convention
`gh pr edit` fails on this repo due to Projects-classic GraphQL; must patch PR body via `gh api -X PATCH .../pulls/<N> -F body=@file`
KAT (known-answer-test) vectors are regenerated by committed `kat_gen` examples/generators and must never be hand-edited; freshness is CI-gated via git diff --exit-code
AGENTS.md 'rule-8' fail-closed asymmetry pattern: encode-side must validate what decode-side hard-rejects (found missing leaf-CID check in `assemble` vs `decode_root`)

code.finding: Public KDF edge functions like settings_ipns_keypair take unvalidated &[u8] secrets; length-floor validation happens at the consumer plane (SessionIdentity::derive in crates/engine/src/session.rs:74-78), not in the KDF layer itself

ROOT_FORMAT_VERSION=1 frozen constant for content DAG root format, distinct namespace from op-record's OP_RECORD_V; the two version concepts never collide because they're reached via different byte-stream paths (op record requires ownerTag/enc/ciphertext fields a DAG root lacks)

OP_RECORD_V=2; op record header is the HPKE AAD directly (not AadContext) since a local journal entry lacks node/scope/epoch; initial design mixed version into AAD only (breaking future format bumps by making old records Undecodable/deleted) until expanded scope added a cleartext v field with type-level-only framing freeze across versions

Test worker hand-assembled EngineWasm object from named imports and cast `as unknown as EngineWasm`, erasing compile-time checks; a new required field (PendingClass) passed typecheck but crashed at runtime only inside the worker — production unaffected since it namespace-imports dynamically

Ship skill's step 7 told workers to poll CodeRabbit checks 'in the background... don't block', causing a lost-wake failure mode where the worker ends its turn and never resumes; fixed to require inline foreground waiting, then found a second instance of the same trap for re-reviews after fix commits

workflow: Parallel worktree agents for independent issues plus a dedicated orchestrator that runs cross-cutting checks (combined-tree compile/test) the individual agents can't see is effective for catching merge-order conflicts before they hit CI

Simulate merges empirically (test-merge branches into a scratch worktree, run cargo check/test) rather than trusting 'textually clean' git merge or GitHub's mergeable badge — repo has been bitten by clean merges that break compile

Background/task-notification workers self-reporting 'done with edges/deps set' should be independently re-verified via API before trusting — three separate ship workers claimed dependency edges they never actually created
Draft PRs let you control CodeRabbit review-slot sequencing manually (hold at draft to avoid stealing a slot; toggle ready when a slot opens) since the review quota is shared org-wide
When restarting a stuck/waiting background agent via SendMessage, the message only lands at the agent's next tool-call round, so it can take a few minutes to take effect if the agent is mid-sleep

friction: First `cargo test --workspace` run for #861 was piped through `tail -40`, truncating output and requiring a full re-run to actually verify results

Ship worker for #863 ended its turn 'standing by' for a ~35 min CodeRabbit cooldown instead of waiting inline — a lost-wake bug where nothing would have resumed it, caught and fixed by restarting with explicit inline-wait instructions

Same lost-wake trap recurred one layer deeper: after CodeRabbit's initial review, the re-review triggered by a fix commit was also rate-limited, and the worker inline-waited ~19 minutes despite having the 'Review rate limited' signal available
Toggling PR #878 to ready happened inside an active CodeRabbit rate-limit window, burning the toggle without buying a review, requiring a second wait-and-retoggle cycle

CodeRabbit's own rate-limit-reset comment timestamp (37 minutes, posted 18:53Z) had to be reconciled against a later slot-claim timestamp reported in local time (UTC+2) by another worker, creating confusion until manually cross-referenced
Multiple ship-worker agents (#862, #876, #879, #880 filings) reported creating GitHub dependency edges that did not actually exist, requiring manual API verification and correction each time

Background Bash commands cap at 10 minutes, so a single wait-then-poll script for CodeRabbit review couldn't cover the full toggle+poll cycle and had to be chained across multiple notification-triggered re-arms
open_items: PR #878 (#864) still pending final merge decision — CI green, both review threads resolved, fix commit b2addfc57 pushed, re-review for that fix commit was rate-limited and the worker was told to stop waiting on it since it's optional polish
